peak_demand_basis: 12% of a 20B-token run (DATASET-DESIGN-reservoir.md §2.1 table row 'QA/forum': 3% default / 12% ceiling)
status: NOT MEASURED — datasets-server rate-limited (per-IP HTTP 429, 13 concurrent recount.py processes). Every token figure below is a CARD-DERIVED estimate, not a dolma2 measurement.

sources.confidence_note: Two recount.py runs (300-sample, seed 0) returned status=FAILED with HTTP 429 on every sampled offset; n_sampled=0, so no tokens/char was measured. The figure here is the card's own 89.7 UTF-8 GB x 0.266 tok/byte, NOT a measurement.
sources.license_evidence: Observed directly in row metadata: metadata.all_licenses == ['Creative Commons - Attribution Share-Alike - https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/'] (2 rows inspected at offset 700000). Card: 'Per-document license information is available in the license entry of the metadata field'. HfApi cardData carries NO license field — the SA fact is only visible per-row.
sources.text_column_chosen_by: verified-by-inspection (not guessed): schema is {added, created, id, metadata:dict, source, text}; `text` is the only payload string column, the other 5 are metadata. No nested payload, so the FinePhrase §3.3 trap does not apply here.
sources.qa_structure_note: Question and answers are NOT in separate columns — the card states 'We use a question, its comments, its answers, and the comments on each answer as a single document', answers ordered by votes with the accepted answer first. Confirmed by inspection: one doc opens with the question title, then body, then comment/answer text concatenated as plain prose (PyMarkdown-flattened). So counting `text` counts the whole Q+A+comments thread exactly once; no cross-column handling was needed.
sources.note: Card figure 23.9B is reproduced exactly by 89.7 GB x 0.266 tok/byte, which is a consistency check on the CARD, not an independent measurement of the corpus.

The unfiltered superset of stackexchange_filtered (33.4M vs 31.0M docs, same dumps). Use ONE of the two, never both. Prefer _filtered.

collections_enumerated.method: HfApi().list_datasets(author='common-pile') — 63 repos, 31 raw/filtered pairs plus comma_v0.1_training_dataset and raw_v0.1_parquet
collections_enumerated.conclusion: common-pile contains exactly ONE large true Q&A corpus (StackExchange). There is no second 10B-scale QA/forum source in the collection, so this category cannot be diversified away from share-alike within common-pile.

category_total_basis: stackexchange_filtered ~23.9B + ubuntu_irc_filtered ~1.4B, both card-bytes-anchored at 0.266 tok/byte. Conservative bound at 0.21 tok/byte: ~19.9B.
meets_3x_peak_demand_note: PROVISIONALLY YES, on card figures only. stackexchange_filtered alone (~23.9B) is 10x the 2.4B peak and 2x the 12B plan pool, and the margin survives the pessimistic 0.21 tok/byte bound (~18.8B, still 7.8x peak). The 3x test is not close enough to the line for the missing measurement to flip it — but the number is unverified and must not be recorded in §3.2 as measured.
overlaps: common-pile/stackexchange (33.4M docs) is the UNFILTERED SUPERSET of common-pile/stackexchange_filtered (31.0M docs) — same Dec-2024 Internet Archive dumps plus the July-2024 official dumps. Never sum them; pick _filtered.

StackExchange dumps are the single most re-derived corpus in open pretraining: the same posts appear in The Pile (StackExchange component), RedPajama, SlimPajama, Dolma, and the datamix1 `stackexchange` category. Any of those entering the reservoir alongside this source double-counts. §2.1's QA/forum pool must be sourced from exactly one StackExchange derivative.

The published 150B corpus in s3://edullm-data is dolma3_mix-150B (see memory), and Dolma mixes carry a StackExchange component — so a reservoir built on stackexchange_filtered overlaps the corpus already published. Not checked (S3 out of scope for this task).
github_archive_filtered is claimed by the `code` pool in §3.2; counting it as QA/forum would double-count across categories.
cccc_filtered overlaps DCLM-baseline / the web pool (both are Common Crawl), and self-reports elevated internal duplication.

share_alike_finding.flag: SHARE-ALIKE, and structurally unavoidable in this category
share_alike_finding.detail: The entire QA/forum pool rests on CC-BY-SA-4.0 content. Unlike `reference` (FineWiki), there is no permissive alternative at 10B scale inside common-pile — ubuntu_irc_filtered is public domain but only ~1.4B tokens, and the one permissive forum-shaped corpus of adequate size (github_archive_filtered, ~10.7B) is already spoken for by the `code` pool.
share_alike_finding.design_impact: §7 item 4 wants FineWiki and StackExchange kept separable in case of publication. Combined with another agent's LibreTexts finding (32% share-alike rows), share-alike is a THIRD source and a larger slice of the reservoir than §7 item 4 assumed. Recommendation: make share-alike a first-class `label` on every entry (queryable at mixture-build time) rather than a per-source note — that is the only way a future 'strip SA and re-mix' request is a metadata query instead of a re-copy. Note this must be decided BEFORE first publish: entry.labels is inside manifest_sha256 and is therefore unbackfillable.
share_alike_finding.if_SA_must_be_dropped: The QA/forum category collapses from ~25B to ~1.4B (ubuntu_irc only), which does NOT meet 3x of the 2.4B peak. This is the single largest license-driven sizing risk found in this category.

needs_streaming_count.why: Rate-limited (HTTP 429, per-IP, 13 concurrent processes) — no tokens/char sample was obtained. Also blocked by the partial-conversion bug below even once the quota recovers.
needs_streaming_count.cheap_retry_first: A 300-sample recount.py run WITH the rows-scaling fix below should settle this in minutes once the quota is free; a Batch streaming count is only needed if /rows stays unavailable.

needs_streaming_count.why: Not attempted (metadata-only by instruction). Parquet conversion is COMPLETE, so recount.py needs no fix for this one — it is the cheapest real number in the category.

tool_bug_found.severity: HIGH — silently understates every partially-converted corpus by ~24x
tool_bug_found.where: artifacts/recount/recount.py main(), `n = per_config[cfg]['num_rows']` (and the same field via /size in combine()'s caller)
tool_bug_found.problem: For these corpora the datasets-server parquet conversion is PARTIAL (`/size` returns `partial: true`). `num_rows` is then only the CONVERTED head, not the split. For stackexchange_filtered: num_rows=1,282,779 converted, estimated_num_rows=27,497,605, card=30,987,814 documents. recount.py multiplies mean_chars x tokens/char by 1.28M and would have reported ~1.1B tokens for a ~24B corpus — a 24x undercount that looks like a clean high-confidence stats-ratio result, because /statistics is ALSO computed over the same partial head so the two estimators AGREE and estimator_divergence stays small.
tool_bug_found.why_it_passes_every_guard: `stats_partial: true` is recorded and downgrades confidence to 'medium' at most — it flags the mean_chars factor as provisional but says nothing about num_rows being the wrong denominator. Nothing in the output reveals the 24x error.
tool_bug_found.affected_in_this_category: stackexchange_filtered (partial, 24x), stackexchange (partial), github_archive_filtered (partial, 23.4M card vs 2.5M converted), cccc_filtered (partial, 6.9M vs 0.9M). NOT affected: ubuntu_irc_filtered, data_provenance_initiative_filtered (both partial=false).
tool_bug_found.fix: Scale by `estimated_num_rows` when `/size` reports `partial: true`, falling back to `num_rows` only when the conversion is complete; record which was used. Note estimated_num_rows is itself ~13% below the card's document count for stackexchange_filtered (27.5M vs 31.0M), so it is an improvement, not ground truth — the card doc count is the better anchor where one exists.
tool_bug_found.affects_other_agents: Any Phase-0 agent whose corpus is large enough to be partially converted has the same 24x exposure. This is worth broadcasting before the §3.2 table is rewritten.

method_caveat_for_this_domain.finding: tokens/char is much LESS stable on Q&A than the README's premise assumes
method_caveat_for_this_domain.evidence: Tokenizing the two real stackexchange_filtered document prefixes obtained before the rate limit (dolma2, locally): a terminal/code-heavy Ubuntu answer ran 0.4524 tok/char, a mostly-prose answer 0.2101 tok/char — a 2.15x spread across two documents in the same corpus.
method_caveat_for_this_domain.why_it_matters: The README justifies the stats-ratio estimator on tokens/char having low CV (~0.27 on FineMath, ~0.1 for English prose). StackExchange documents interleave prose with code blocks, shell transcripts, tracebacks and markdown tables, so the per-document tok/char CV here should be expected to be substantially higher than on prose corpora. n=2 is anecdote, not a measurement — but whoever re-runs this should READ `tokens_per_char_cv` in the output rather than assume the prose prior, and consider raising --n-sample above 300 if it comes back high.
method_caveat_for_this_domain.direction_of_error: Unknown sign, but it widens the interval around any stats-ratio figure for this category specifically.
